# Runtime conformance fixtures

Generated by [`gen/generate.py`](./gen/generate.py). Don't edit the JSON by hand: change the
generator and run it (`python3 runtimes/testdata/gen/generate.py`). CI runs it with `--check` and
fails on drift. It needs `jsonschema` and `cryptography`. Every artifact message is validated
against the MF2 data-model schema, and every manifest and artifact against [`schemas/`](./schemas).

## `scenarios/*.json` (resolution, SPEC §4–§6)

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `manifest` | A v1 manifest (unsigned; resolution doesn't involve signatures) |
| `artifacts` | `{ sha256: "<exact artifact bytes>" }`. Hash the string's UTF-8 bytes |
| `cases[].requested` | Locales in priority order, already the resolver chain's output (canonicalize them, SPEC §4.1) |
| `cases[].id`, `values` | Message to render, and its arguments |
| `cases[].default` | Inline default at the call site, if any |
| `cases[].bidiIsolation` | Always `"none"` here, so expectations carry no isolation marks |
| `cases[].exp` | Rendered string |
| `cases[].expLocale`, `expChain`, `expResolvedFrom` | What `explain()` must report (`expResolvedFrom: null` = inline default) |
| `cases[].expDirection` | When present, the direction exposed for the active locale |

## `loading/*.json` (reliability, SPEC §1.3, §3)

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `publicKeys` | `[{keyId, key}]` with the key as base64url raw Ed25519 public key; empty = verification off |
| `steps[].edge.manifest` | The edge's answer to the manifest request: `{status: 200, etag, body}`, `{status: 304}` or an error status |
| `steps[].edge.artifacts` | `{ sha256: "<bytes served for that path>" }`; a missing hash answers 404. Bytes may deliberately not match their hash |
| `steps[].read` | After the step's refresh settles, render `id` for `requested` |
| `steps[].exp` | Expected rendered string |
| `steps[].expActiveRelease` | Active release ID afterwards, or `null` when nothing is active |
| `steps[].expSource` | `explain().source` for the read |
| `steps[].expErrors` | Error `type`s emitted during the step, in order |
| `restartBefore` | Step indexes before which the runtime restarts: memory is dropped, persisted storage kept |
| `installationId` | Staged rollout (SPEC §1.4): the installation id the runtime must use, as if it had created and persisted it. Absent = the runtime's own |
| `rolloutSupport` | `false` = run with rollout support turned off (SPEC §1.4); absent = on |
| `steps[].expRollout` | `explain().rollout` for the read: `{id, percent, cohort, side}` or `null` |

Each loading file starts with empty persisted storage. The Ed25519 key that signs these
fixtures is a fixed, test-only key (seed in the generator); it signs nothing else.

The `rollout-*.json` sequences: `rollout-old-runtime` (support off, the rollout at 100 %, an
installation inside the candidate: still stable, no candidate fetch) and `rollout-stable-side` (an
installation outside the candidate through start, restart, advance and abort) pass in every
runtime, including one written before SPEC §1.4, by ignoring `rollout`, which is the old-runtime
guarantee itself. `rollout-candidate-side` (activation, restart, advance, abort back to stable, a
new rollout drawing again), `rollout-candidate-fallback` (a candidate whose artifact fails
integrity falls back to the stable view of the same manifest) and `rollout-invalid` (an invalid
`rollout` is ignored with a `schema` error) need §1.4: JS and Go pass them since RFC 0006 wave 2,
Dart since wave 3.

## `rollout/cohorts.json` (staged rollout, SPEC §1.4)

Not a loading sequence: the table a runtime checks its cohort function against, id by id, and
the ids RFC 0006 §12.4 drives three runtimes with. The generator computes every cohort from
SPEC §1.4's formula with `hashlib`, and imports, ports or copies nothing from any runtime.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `salt` | The rollout salt every `installations` entry is hashed with |
| `installations` | `[installationId, cohort]` × 10,000 |
| `expCandidates` | `{percent: n}`: how many of `installations` are in the candidate at that percentage (`cohort < percent × 100`) |
| `vectors[]` | `{salt, key, cohort, note}`: SPEC §1.4's test vectors, the cohorts at the 1 % and 10 % boundaries, another salt, and Go per-request keys (non-ASCII, case, NFD vs NFC) |

## `edge/*.json` (delivery-key scopes, SPEC §2)

For `glossa-edge`, not the runtimes. Every key index object is validated against
[`schemas/delivery-key.schema.json`](./schemas/delivery-key.schema.json).

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `project` | The project every key belongs to |
| `keys` | `{ label: {key, index} }`: a publishable key and its index object, stored at `v1/keys/<sha256(key)>.json`. `index: null` means no object (a revoked key) |
| `environments` | Environments that have a manifest in storage |
| `cases[].key`, `environment` | Request `GET /v1/{keys[key].key}/{environment}/manifest.json` |
| `cases[].artifact` | When `true`, request an artifact of the project instead |
| `cases[].expStatus` | `200`, or `404` with exactly the body an unknown key gets |

## `usages/` (context, RFC 0004 §2.1)

This is the shared fixture suite for `@klarlabs-studio/glossa/unplugin` and `glossa extract`: source trees, and the
`glossa.usages/v1` document each tool must produce from them. These `expected.json` files are
written by hand, unlike the generated files above. [`gen/check_usages.py`](./gen/check_usages.py)
validates them. It also validates `schemas/usages.v1.schema.json`,
`schemas/captures.v1.schema.json`, `schemas/finding.v1.schema.json` and their
[`examples/`](./schemas/examples). CI runs it next to `generate.py --check`. The contract itself is in [`usages/README.md`](./usages/README.md).

## `markup.json` (formatted parts → HTML, SPEC §5)

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `safeTags` | The only markup names that become HTML elements. `@klarlabs-studio/glossa/elements` (`SAFE_TAGS`) and the Go runtime (`HTML`, `th`) are tested against this list |
| `voidTags` | Safe tags rendered without children or a closing tag (`<br>`) |
| `cases[].parts` | Formatted parts in the MF2 shape (`text`, `markup`, `bidiIsolation`, `string`, `number` with `parts`, `fallback` with `source`) |
| `cases[].html` | Expected HTML: markup options dropped, text escaped (`&`, `<`, `>`), unsafe markup reduced to its content |
